summary: Max Walleser was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the universities of Freiburg, Geneva, Heidelberg, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D.). He served as a Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936) at Heidelberg University.

Max Weber worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, Göttingen, and Berlin, he held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1896), Heidelberg University (~1896–1918), the University of Vienna (~1918), and the University of Munich (~1919–1920).
Maximilian Bittner was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna from ~1887 to ~1893, including under Friedrich Müller.
Maximilian Enger specialized in Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (~1848–1851), where he later served as a Privatdozent from 1852 to 1861.

Maximilian Hoth is an Indologist who completed an MA at the University of Hamburg (2023–2025) and studied at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities. He became a PhD candidate at the University of Munich in 2026.
May Oung was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Cambridge from ~1904 to ~1907. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Cambridge, Yale (Ph.D.), and Harvard University. She taught at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a history professor at Harvard University around 2009.
Maya Keller-Grimm was a Buddhist studies scholar. From around 1970 to 1990, she served as leader of the Altbuddhistische Gemeinde and editor of Yāna.
Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a General Council member there from 1964 to 1965.

Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She taught at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and was appointed specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Małgorzata Sulich-Cowley is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, the University of Lausanne, and the University of Warsaw (PhD). She held posts at SWPS University (2015) and the University of Warsaw (2018–2021).
McComas Taylor is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University, where he was appointed Emeritus Professor in 2005.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Clyde Kluckhohn, at Harvard, and at the University of Chicago (PhD). He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at Chicago from ~1955 to ~1998.

Md Mohiuddin Ahmed Tanvir studied religious and Buddhist studies, earning a BA from the University of Dhaka (2019–2023). He held counsellor posts at AHZ Bangladesh (2024–2025), IDP Education (2025–2026), and Kampus Group (2026).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing (PhD). In 2008, he held lectureships at Colombo, Pali and Buddhist Studies, and BPUSL.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She received her PhD from Stanford University in 2010 and was an associate professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, in 2017.
Megumu Honda was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and holds a professorship at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962) and served there as a professor (attested 1963–1971 and 2007).
